Title: Retrieve a file with an empty folder name in the path
Preconditions: A file named 'test.jpg' exists in the 'tailor-photos' bucket under a folder named 'valid-folder'
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /{folder}/{fileName} with the path variables set to empty string for folder and 'test.jpg' for fileName.

Test Data: folder: "", fileName: "test.jpg"
Expected Result: The API responds with a 404 Not Found status code, and no file is returned.

Title: Retrieve a file with an empty file name in the path
Preconditions: A file named 'test.jpg' exists in the 'tailor-photos' bucket under a folder named 'valid-folder'
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /{folder}/{fileName} with the path variables set to 'valid-folder' for folder and empty string for fileName.

Test Data: folder: "valid-folder", fileName: ""
Expected Result: The API responds with a 404 Not Found status code, and no file is returned.

Expected Result: The API responds with a 404 Not Found status code, and no file is returned.

Test Data: folder: "valid-folder", fileName: "a" repeated 250 times + ".jpg"
Expected Result: The API responds with a 404 Not Found status code, and no file is returned.

Steps:

Test Data: folder: orders, fileName: sample.jpg

Title: Request file that does not exist in MinIO storage
Preconditions: The application service and MinIO instance are running
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /photos/nonexistent-file.jpg.

Test Data: folder: photos, fileName: nonexistent-file.jpg
Expected Result: The system returns an HTTP 404 Not Found response status code.

Title: Verify that path traversal sequences in folder and fileName parameters are rejected without exposing internal file system contents or sensitive server details
Preconditions: The application is running and connected to the object storage service
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /..%2F..%2Fetc/passwd with folder set to '..%2F..' and fileName set to 'passwd'.

Test Data: folder = '..%2F..', fileName = 'passwd'
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found). The response body does not contain internal system files, stack traces, or storage credentials.

Title: Verify that requesting a non-existent or invalid object path does not leak MinIO storage credentials or internal exception details
Preconditions: The application is running and connected to the object storage service
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /invalid-folder/non-existent-file.jpg.

Test Data: folder = 'invalid-folder', fileName = 'non-existent-file.jpg'
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found). The response body is empty or contains standard error formatting, with no exposure of internal MinIO client configuration or secret keys.
